newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - April 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - April 4.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Friday:
* Hundreds of America Online subscribers have complained about unexpected charges on their bills related to their use of an "800" number to gain access to the service.
* Market place: Chief executives who received stock options did not exercise many of them during 1996.
* Saudi Arabia's Prince al-Waleed bin Talal, who now owns more than five percent of Apple Computer, said he believed the computer maker had a strong franchise and loyal customers.
* Disney's ABC has withdrawn from negotiations with Carsey-Werner productions over a new Roseanne comedy series, executives close to the talks say.
* The Federal Communications Commission voted to lend the country's television stations a second channel to broadcast digital versions of programming.
* The Dow Jones industrials closed down 39.66 points at 6,477.35.
* March car and truck sales were the strongest in at least eight years.
* Liggett Group and California reached a pact that would include California in the company's lawsuit settlement with other states seeking reimbursement for tobacco-related Medicaid expenses.
* Disney said it bought a controlling stake in Starwave Corp, the Internet publisher owned by Microsoft co-founder Paul Allen.
* The prices of short-term Treasury securities rose after the Fed entered the market to buy bills.
* Channel Tunnel operators promised new safety measures to prevent another fire breaking out in the tunnel connecting Britain to continental Europe.
* Advertising: California has stepped up its anti-tobacco campaign, worried about more smokers in the state.
* McDonalds Campaign 55, which reduces prices on various sandwiches to $0.55, creates the illusion of value pricing without a steep markdown which would hurt profitability.
